1.name: DB Schema (Categories, Inventory, Badges, RLS)
notes: I do not have Postgres/DB credentials (only VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, not the DB password or a Management API token), so schema DDL can't be run by me directly -- user ran supabase/schema.sql in the Supabase SQL Editor.

supabase/schema.sql: idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS / ON CONFLICT / DROP POLICY IF EXISTS) so safe to re-run. Creates profiles, categories (seeded), inventory_items, badges, user_badges. Enables RLS + auth.uid()-based policies on profiles/inventory_items/user_badges only -- categories/badges are shared reference data, intentionally left without RLS.
user_badges has no update/delete policy by design -- earned badges are append-only for the client; default-deny (no policy = no access) covers this, not an oversight.

RLS verified via supabase/test_rls.sql with 2 real test auth users: impersonating test-a (id 1d238dc5-ba60-4ee6-b635-3c35485cbd63) returned only 'Test A milk'; impersonating test-b (id eacc0de3-fd86-4e45-9ff1-ace47bdf2d24) returned only 'Test B chips'. Isolation confirmed both directions. Test rows cleaned up afterward; the two test auth users/profiles were left in place (harmless, deletable later).
MODULE 1 COMPLETE 2026-08-13.
2026-08-19 OPUS AUDIT: found 7 issues in the original schema; fixes written to supabase/002_hardening.sql (must be run in SQL Editor after schema.sql).

AUDIT-1 (CRITICAL, empirically verified): categories and badges had RLS disabled on the wrong assumption that 'reference data doesn't need RLS'. Supabase exposes all public-schema tables via PostgREST and grants anon/authenticated write privileges by default, so RLS-off = writes allowed. Proven live against this project using ONLY the anon key (public, ships in the frontend bundle): POST /rest/v1/categories -> 201, DELETE -> 204, POST /rest/v1/badges -> 201. Any visitor could rename/delete everyone's categories or badges. Fixed by enabling RLS + SELECT-only policy on both. Audit test rows were cleaned up; tables verified back to original state (categories ids 1-5, badges empty).

AUDIT-2: created_at/used_at/earned_at were `timestamp` (no tz). now() is timestamptz and gets silently flattened to UTC. In an IST (UTC+5:30) date-deadline app this causes off-by-one-day errors near midnight. Converted to timestamptz. expiry_date deliberately stays `date` -- a printed best-before is a calendar date, not an instant.

AUDIT-3: FKs to auth.users had no ON DELETE, defaulting to NO ACTION -- deleting a user with any inventory row would fail with an FK violation. Now ON DELETE CASCADE. category_id -> ON DELETE SET NULL (retiring a category must not delete the user's food). badge_id -> CASCADE.

AUDIT-4: profiles row was to be inserted client-side after signUp() (Module 2 plan). Fragile (crash between the two calls orphans the auth user) and doesn't work for Google OAuth, which returns from redirect already authenticated with no 'just signed up' hook. Replaced with an AFTER INSERT trigger on auth.users (public.handle_new_user, security definer, search_path pinned to ''). Existing users backfilled. >>> MODULE 2 MUST NOT insert into profiles -- the trigger owns it.

AUDIT-5: no indexes on the columns RLS puts in EVERY query's WHERE clause. Added (user_id,status) for Module 4's list, partial (expiry_date) where status='active' for Module 8's cron scan, and (user_id) on user_badges.

AUDIT-6: bare auth.uid() in policies re-evaluates per row; wrapped in (select auth.uid()) so the planner hoists it to an InitPlan (Supabase's documented RLS perf guidance). Also made WITH CHECK explicit on UPDATE policies -- note this was NOT a hole before, Postgres falls back to the USING expression when WITH CHECK is omitted.
AUDIT-7: added check (quantity > 0). Module 3's React Hook Form validation is UX, not enforcement -- the REST endpoint is public.

AUDIT-DEFERRED (design decision, revisit at Module 9): profiles.points and user_badges remain directly writable by their owner, so a user can set their own points or award themselves badges from devtools, bypassing the client-side criteria logic. Fix if wanted: revoke update(points) from authenticated + move awards into SECURITY DEFINER functions. Left as-is for now since Module 9's reward logic doesn't exist yet and this is a trust-the-user college project.

notes: PARSER DESIGN -- the ordering is load-bearing. Quantity+unit is matched FIRST, and any chrono date hit overlapping that span is discarded. Without this, chrono reads the 'two' in 'two packs of milk' as 2 o'clock, swallows the number, and the quantity silently vanishes. There's a regression test for exactly this ('does not mistake a spoken quantity for a clock time').

PARSER -- transcript is lowercased but NEVER re-spaced before regex matching, because collapsing whitespace would shift string indices out of alignment with what chrono sees, corrupting the span arithmetic used to cut the name out.
PARSER -- chrono runs with forwardDate:true so '25th August' means the upcoming one (expiry dates are future-facing).
PARSER -- follows the roadmap's 'blank is safer than wrong' rule: unrecognised fields stay null for the user to fill on Verify rather than being guessed.

PARSER BUG FOUND AND FIXED BY THE TESTS: the bare-number fallback originally matched digits only, so 'three bottles' silently dropped the quantity ('bottles' isn't one of the six DB units so the quantity+unit rule didn't fire either). Now matches number words too. 'a'/'an' are deliberately excluded from the bare path -- alone they're articles, not counts -- but still count when bound to a real unit ('a packet of bread'). This is exactly the class of bug the user's decision to add tests caught.
BUNDLE: chrono-node correctly code-split into its own chunk (175kB raw / 43kB gzipped, emitted as assets/esm-*.js); app shell only grew ~8kB.

>>> FINDING FOR MODULE 6: the Workbox globPatterns ['**/*.{js,...}'] precaches EVERY emitted JS chunk including lazily-imported ones. So dynamic import() keeps a lib out of the app-shell bundle, but the service worker still downloads it at install time. Acceptable for chrono (43kB, and it buys offline voice parsing) but it would completely undo the Module 0 lazy-load decision for Tesseract.js/OpenCV.js. Exclude those chunks from globPatterns when Module 6 lands. Note added inline in vite.config.js.
CANNOT SELF-VERIFY: speech recognition needs a real microphone and a browser; there is no headless path. The parser is fully tested, the wrapper and UI are not. Browser test script is in PROGRESS.md.

6.name: OCR / Camera Scanning (PHASE 1)

decisions.canvas_preprocessing_not_opencv: User chose Canvas 2D preprocessing over OpenCV.js. Greyscale + 2x upscale + percentile contrast stretch is ~40 lines with zero dependencies and covers what actually helps Tesseract on faint date printing. OpenCV's real value is deskew/perspective correction -- revisit only if real photos prove it's needed, rather than paying ~8MB preemptively.
decisions.phased_build: User chose to build the core path first (camera -> preprocess -> Tesseract -> date parse -> Verify) and defer OCR.space fallback + ZXing barcode to phase 2, so accuracy can be measured on real packaging before adding more subsystems.
decisions.ocrspace_deferred: User chose to defer the OCR.space API key. Low-confidence reads currently surface an explicit warning on the Verify screen instead of silently falling back. CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD=60 in src/lib/ocr.js is where the fallback hooks in.
decisions.no_name_extraction_from_ocr: parseOcrText deliberately does NOT guess the product name. OCR of packaging picks up marketing copy, nutrition tables and legal small print; a confidently wrong name is worse than a blank field. The barcode path (phase 2) is the reliable name source -- barcodes carry product identity even when printed dates are unreadable.

notes: PARSER -- DD/MM is assumed (Indian packaging), but flips to MM/DD when the numbers rule it out (e.g. 03/15/2027, where 15 can't be a month).

PARSER -- month-only dates resolve by context: an expiry 'EXP 03/2027' becomes the LAST day of March (the product is good through the month), while a manufacturing date used for relative-shelf-life maths becomes the FIRST day (earliest plausible make-date, so the computed expiry errs early/safe).
PARSER -- addMonths clamps the day, so '31/12/2026 BEST BEFORE 2 MONTHS' gives 2027-02-28 rather than JS Date's default roll-over to 3 March. Covered by a test.

PARSER BUG #1 FOUND BY TESTS: an implausible date like '31/02/2027' was rejected as a whole, but the looser month-year pattern then scavenged '02/2027' out of the middle of it and returned end-of-February. Fixed by claiming the matched span even when the date is rejected -- salvaging a fragment of text just judged invalid is exactly how a confident wrong date gets produced.

PARSER BUG #2 FOUND BY TESTS (a real latent bug, exposed by fixing #1): the alpha-month pattern matched ANY three letters, so 'MFG 01/2026 EXP 01/2028' parsed as '26 EXP 01' -- reading the label itself as a month name and swallowing both real dates. Fixed by baking the twelve month abbreviations into the regex instead of validating after the match.

BUNDLE -- verified empirically: dist contains NO .wasm and NO traineddata. Only a ~17kB tesseract.js wrapper reaches dist (emitted as assets/src-*.js, NOT tesseract*.js -- an earlier globIgnores pattern silently failed to match because of this). Tesseract fetches worker.min.js, the ~4MB WASM core and language data from cdn.jsdelivr.net at runtime. So the Module 5 precache worry turned out to be moot here; the ineffective globIgnores was removed and the comment corrected rather than left claiming a protection that wasn't real.

CONSEQUENCE FOR MODULE 10 (PWA offline): scanning requires a network connection and a reachable jsdelivr CDN. OCR will NOT work offline. Voice also needs network (Chrome's speech recognition is server-side). Only manual entry is truly offline-capable.

CANNOT SELF-VERIFY: camera capture and real OCR accuracy need a physical camera and real packaging. The text parser and histogram maths are fully unit-tested; the camera pipeline and actual recognition quality are not. Browser test script in PROGRESS.md.

C_performance: C1: Tesseract.recognize() creates a worker and terminates it in a `finally` on EVERY call (confirmed by reading node_modules/tesseract.js/src/Tesseract.js), so each scan re-spun the worker and reloaded language data. Now a module-level createWorker('eng') singleton plus disposeOcr() called from ScanItem's unmount, so only the first scan of a session pays init cost. A failed init deliberately does NOT cache its rejection, or the scanner could never recover without a page reload.
